domain: Subtraction of fractions and mixed numbers, including normalization, denominator alignment, regrouping, and final simplification/expression

skills.name: Normalize mixed forms
skills.definition: Rewrite a mixed number with an improper fractional part into an equivalent standard mixed number before subtraction.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a step explicitly converts a form like 2 3/2 or 1 4/3 into a standard mixed number.
Tag when the solver states that a mixed number is normalized because its fractional part is improper.
Tag only when the mixed-number structure changes due to an improper fractional part.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when a whole number is rewritten as n + 0/d.
Do not tag for finding a common denominator or converting to equivalent fractions for denominator matching.
Do not tag for borrowing/regrouping during subtraction.

skills.name: Align denominators
skills.definition: Find a common denominator and rewrite fraction parts as equivalent fractions with that denominator before subtraction.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when the solution finds an LCD or common denominator for unlike denominators.
Tag when fraction parts are converted to equivalent fractions to prepare for subtraction, including within mixed numbers.
Tag when the solution explicitly checks denominators and states they are already common.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when denominators are already the same and no denominator-alignment step is shown.
Do not tag for subtracting numerators or whole-number parts after setup.
Do not tag for simplification or final answer expression.

skills.name: Subtract fraction parts
skills.definition: Subtract fractional quantities once they are in compatible form, including same-denominator fraction subtraction within fraction-only or mixed-number problems.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when numerators are subtracted over a shared denominator.
Tag for pure fraction subtraction such as 6/7 − 4/7 or 6/8 − 3/8.
Tag for subtracting the fractional parts of mixed numbers before or after any needed borrowing adjustment.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag for finding the common denominator itself.
Do not tag for subtracting whole-number parts.
Do not tag for the regrouping step that borrows 1 whole and converts it to fractional units.

skills.name: Subtract whole parts
skills.definition: Subtract the whole-number components of mixed numbers or rewritten whole-plus-fraction forms.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when the solution explicitly computes the whole-part difference, such as 4 − 3 = 1.
Tag when a whole number is treated as the whole component in a mixed-number subtraction setup.
Tag whether or not borrowing is later needed.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag for fraction-only items with no whole-number component.
Do not tag for borrowing steps that adjust the whole part after an initial subtraction.
Do not tag for merely combining final whole and fractional results into one answer.

skills.name: Borrow across whole
skills.definition: Regroup one whole as fractional units and adjust the whole part when the fractional subtraction would otherwise be negative or insufficient.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when the solution borrows 1 from the whole part to continue subtraction.
Tag when 1 whole is converted into d/d and added to the fractional part.
Tag when a whole-number or mixed-number minuend is rewritten with 0/d and then regrouped as part of borrowing.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when no regrouping is needed.
Do not tag for ordinary subtraction of whole parts or fraction parts without borrowing.
Do not tag for simplification after regrouping is complete.

skills.name: Simplify and express
skills.definition: Reduce the result to lowest terms and present it in an appropriate final form such as a fraction, mixed number, whole number, or 0.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a fraction is reduced, such as 2/10 to 1/5 or 9/12 to 3/4.
Tag when 0 over a denominator is simplified to 0 or a zero fractional part is absorbed into a whole number.
Tag when computed whole and fractional parts are combined into the reported final answer.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag for arithmetic subtraction steps themselves.
Do not tag for finding common denominators, normalization, or borrowing.
Do not tag when no simplification or final-form expression step is shown.
